title: Delta-aware latency canary for PR benchmarking
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce a delta-aware latency canary that runs lightweight synthetic workloads in PR CI to detect statistically significant regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency. This ticket covers the harness design, CI integration, and abort criteria so PRs with performance regressions can be gated automatically. The goal is a low-noise, low-cost detector that differentiates true regressions from sample variance and cache-warmup effects.
acceptance_criteria: Canary job runs as part of the PR pipeline and finishes within 6 minutes on average
Detector reports tokens/sec and p95 for configured model variants and emits a clear pass/fail verdict
False positive rate under normal noise < 2% on historical PRs (measured against last 90 days of benchmarks)
Blocked PRs include a link to a diagnostics artifact (trace + sample requests + histogram) and clear remediation guidance
Integration with GitHub checks: failing canary marks the PR check as failed with actionable message
design_notes: Key ideas: 1) Use small ensembles of synthetic requests that target common execution paths: short/long sequences, cache hit/miss, multibatch versus single request. 2) Maintain a rolling baseline per model-variant computed from the last N successful CI runs (N configurable, default 50). 3) Apply a delta-test using sequential hypothesis testing (two-sided CUSUM + optional Bayesian posterior check) to detect upward shifts in p95 and downward shifts in tokens/sec. 4) Account for warm-up by ignoring the first M requests (configurable) and by running a short warm-up phase inside the job. 5) Produce per-request traces and aggregate histograms (p50,p90,p95,p99,tail) and token throughput. 6) Provide tunable sensitivity per project: production-critical models get stricter thresholds. 7) Store artifacts in S3 and surface links in the CI check. 8) Implement throttling so the canary can run in both Hosted and Dedicated CI pools without causing capacity pressure.
plan: Prototype synthetic workload generator (go/python) that emits deterministic token streams and sequence length distributions
Implement baseline store: time-series-backed baseline that keeps last 50 successful run metrics per model-variant
Implement statistical detector service that consumes current run metrics and baseline and returns pass/fail + confidence score
Integrate canary as a GitHub Action job step and expose config via repo-level redwood-ci.yaml
Add diagnostics artifact packaging: perf histograms, sample requests, kernel selection logs
Run alpha on internal infra repos for 2 weeks, measure FP/FN; iterate thresholds
Rollout: opt-in for all engineering repos, then enable gating for high-traffic runtime changes
